stories.title: MedChemBench separates scientific explanation from compound selection
stories.alt: Conceptual panel distinguishing molecular structure and evidence reasoning from compound selection and property prediction; historical benchmarking is explicitly separated from laboratory validation.
stories.facts: OpenAI introduced MedChemBench, with 99 problems drawn from published medicinal-chemistry research. It evaluates molecular reconstruction, explanations, compound selection and property prediction; selection and numerical prediction remain difficult.
stories.inference: Evaluate assistants by downstream decision quality as well as explanation quality. For research automation, test the full evidence-to-action pipeline rather than relying on one aggregate score.
stories.uncertainty: Prior exposure to published sources cannot be ruled out. Benchmark results do not establish new-drug discovery or improved laboratory decisions.

stories.title: Pairs-trading preprint exposes a gap between utility and wealth moments
stories.alt: Conceptual panel showing an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck spread model, an optimal feedback policy with finite expected utility, and infinite expected terminal wealth under some parameter and horizon conditions; no market return forecast is shown.
stories.facts: Aleksei Kozhevnikov derives optimal feedback for a finite-horizon pairs model with an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck spread and negative-power utility. Under specified parameter and horizon conditions, expected terminal wealth is infinite while optimal expected utility remains finite.
stories.inference: Inspect tail moments and sensitivity to mean-reversion estimates alongside reward or utility. Reject an apparent optimum that depends on unrealistic tails or unstable exposure.
stories.uncertainty: A theoretical preprint, not peer-reviewed live-trading evidence. Its admissible nonnegative-wealth model is not a real-world capital guarantee; borrow, slippage and model error require separate tests.

stories.title: Anthropic’s underwriters exercise IPO option; support changes
stories.date: Company announcement and Reuters report November 20, 2026
stories.alt: Conceptual panel showing the IPO option fully exercised through purchase of extra issuer shares, with that option no longer available for open-market covering support; no price floor is implied.
stories.facts: Anthropic confirmed full exercise of the underwriters’ option for 147 million additional shares at the IPO price. Reuters reported that closing this stabilization position removed one potential source of open-market buying support.
stories.inference: Treat IPO stabilization as a temporary mechanism, never a price floor. Separate single-name event exposure from SPY/QQQ signals; verify actual ETF holdings before assuming direct index exposure.
stories.uncertainty: No continuing support level, dealer gamma, index inclusion or next-session price direction was verified.

stories.title: GDP and October PCE share Wednesday’s premarket release window
stories.date: BEA calendar updated November 20; releases scheduled November 25, 2026
nodes:
SAME RELEASE TIME
October income / PCE

Scheduled releases
Results not yet known
stories.alt: Calendar panel showing November 25 at 7:30 a.m. CST for third-quarter GDP second estimate and October personal income and outlays, explicitly labeled scheduled releases with results unknown.
stories.facts: BEA schedules the third-quarter GDP second estimate and corporate profits alongside October Personal Income and Outlays for November 25 at 8:30 a.m. Eastern, or 7:30 a.m. Central. The latter release contains PCE inflation measures.
stories.inference: Model a joint growth-and-inflation event window: avoid treating simultaneous surprises as independent signals, and refresh execution assumptions after the releases.
stories.uncertainty: This is a verified upcoming calendar event, not released data, a consensus estimate or a forecast of Fed action. Schedules can change.

stories.title: Samsung puts memory-development leader in charge of the business
nodes:
Sang Joon Hwang
Promoted to president
stories.alt: Leadership panel showing Sang Joon Hwang promoted to president and moving from head of memory development to head of Samsung’s Memory Business.
stories.facts: Samsung promoted Sang Joon Hwang to president and named him head of its Memory Business. He previously led memory development, including DRAM and high-bandwidth memory.
stories.inference: Track product qualification, delivery and margins when assessing memory suppliers; a leadership appointment alone is insufficient evidence of better operating performance.
stories.uncertainty: The announcement provides no new shipment, yield, customer-qualification or earnings result.
